summary: August 29 production recovered through a six-package takeover and completed Phase B, promotion, response, and DONE closure after the morning bundle failure. The evidence pack's prior-day trending repair alarm remains acknowledged against the active orchestration and reliability backlog rather than being re-filed. Saturday's workflow read found two fail-open control paths: daily auto-pause state can fail to persist while the run continues, and the retro can stay green after every evidence-producing step fails. Four live runbooks also advertise retired Phase B backstop times, while the workflow supply chain still depends on mutable action tags. Performance remains too thin and recovery-distorted to justify a new cadence, format-mix, or topic-direction change; the existing no-change strategy backlog already owns that decision.

alarm_ack.production_repair_trending: Acknowledged against active critical backlog 2fc5cbb21cca and reliability/mix backlog 33ccbcdc479b. The alarm describes the August 28 repair snapshot in doctor/evidence.json; August 29 subsequently recovered through takeover authoring, passed Phase B with 6 accepted and 0 rejected, and committed response.json plus DONE, so duplicating the historical outage would add no new repair owner.

findings.title: Auto-pause state can disappear while Daily keeps going
findings.observation: Both branches that change the bounded auto-pause state append `|| true` to ci_commit_state.sh. A rejected push or transient commit failure therefore leaves only runner-local failure_count.txt or auto_pause_day.txt changes, yet preflight still emits skip=auto or resumes the run. The next firing reads the old committed state and can repeat the wrong branch, defeating the promised one-day pause and automatic retry semantics.
findings.proposal: Make persistence of auto_pause_day.txt and failure_count.txt a required preflight outcome. If the state commit fails, stop before publishing or claiming a durable pause, emit a named infrastructure failure, and add an executable test covering rejected persistence on both the pause and resume branches.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/daily.yml:153-174 writes the pause/resume files, calls scripts/ci_commit_state.sh with `|| true` in both branches, and then sets the control output without checking that main contains the new state.

findings.title: Four runbooks still publish retired Phase B times
findings.observation: The live Phase B workflow now uses paired UTC crons plus an America/Chicago gate for 08:30 Central, but operator-facing instructions still name two retired schedules: README.md says 06:15 UTC, while FALLBACKS, exchange/README, and CLAUDE_ROUTINE_INSTRUCTIONS say 12:45 UTC. FALLBACKS also contradicts itself by later documenting the current DST-aware 08:30 rule.
findings.proposal: Replace every retired fixed-UTC claim with the canonical 08:30 America/Chicago contract, link the prose to exchange_phase_b.yml as the executable authority, and add a lightweight documentation test that rejects the retired 06:15 UTC and 12:45 UTC phrases in active runbooks.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/exchange_phase_b.yml:69-71 schedules 13:30 and 14:30 UTC candidates and gates them in America/Chicago. README.md:32-33 says 06:15 UTC; docs/FALLBACKS.md:85-86 says 12:45 UTC while line 220 says DST-aware 08:30; exchange/README.md:450-452 and CLAUDE_ROUTINE_INSTRUCTIONS.md:73-82 still say 12:45 UTC.

findings.title: Retro can publish green after losing its evidence pack
findings.observation: Advance-experiments, failure-census, brief construction, and proposal triage all use continue-on-error=true. The final commit step is fail-closed only around whatever files happen to exist, so build_retro.py and review_proposals.py can both fail while ci_commit_state.sh finds old or unrelated state and the workflow still finishes green. That turns absence of the day's brief or triage into a silent success.
findings.proposal: Keep analytics refresh best-effort, but make brief construction and triage required for the modes that invoke them. Add an explicit artifact gate before commit that checks the resolved date, freshness, schema, and required brief/triage files; fail only after preserving diagnostics so a missing daily review is visible and retryable.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/retro.yml:128-181 marks experiment advance, failure census, Build the brief, and Triage proposals continue-on-error; lines 194-211 commit without first asserting fresh outputs. scripts/build_retro.py documents required retro/<date>/brief.json and brief.md outputs, while scripts/review_proposals.py documents triage.json as its durable result.

findings.title: Workflow dependencies still float on mutable action tags
findings.observation: Production, review, diagnosis, and exchange workflows invoke actions/checkout@v4 and actions/setup-python@v5 by mutable major-version tags. A compromised or unexpectedly changed upstream tag can alter code executed with contents:write permissions without any repository commit changing, making an incident hard to reproduce or audit.
findings.proposal: Adopt a repository-wide action pinning policy: replace mutable tags with reviewed full commit SHAs, retain the human-readable release in comments, and use Dependabot or Renovate to propose auditable update pull requests with the normal workflow tests.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/daily.yml, .github/workflows/retro.yml, .github/workflows/doctor.yml, and .github/workflows/exchange_phase_b.yml all use actions/checkout@v4 and/or actions/setup-python@v5 while their jobs hold write-capable repository permissions.
